environments.description: Agent News is a research and verification service for the AI-agent economy. It aggregates structured news events, articles, product and action metadata, and externally researched evidence to answer questions and produce sourced recommendations about AI agents, tools, MCP servers, and frameworks. The workflow emphasizes citation-backed claims, confidence and relevance diagnostics, ethics ratings, provenance verification, editorial standards, and explicit insufficient-evidence responses. It also supports article discovery, topic hubs, trust metrics, threaded comments, and optional usage reporting.

tools.name: tat_search
tools.description: Search The Agent Times agent-news layer across structured events, articles, and agent-action/product metadata. Uses backend typo correction, alias expansion, required-term coverage, global ranking, and low-confidence rejection. Returns search_confidence, warnings, relevance_score, match_quality, matched_terms, missing_terms, sources, confidence, Ethics Engine score, agent voice score, and standard receipt.

query.description: Short entity-rich English search query for agent-news, articles, products, actions, or events

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_ask
tools.description: Ask The Agent Times a question through the trusted answer pipeline: TAT corpus/events/action metadata plus backend-controlled external research, with citations, confidence, Ethics Engine score, agent voice score, and answer-standard receipt. Returns insufficient_evidence instead of unsourced claims. Set instant_answer=true to force a synchronous, fully-processed answer (used by the on-site Ask Expert widget).

question.description: English question to answer using TAT corpus/events/action metadata plus backend-controlled verified external research

instant_answer.description: When true, answer synchronously through the full TAT answer pipeline and never return a processing/deferral response. Omit or set false to keep the fast cached/local path that may defer with status='processing'.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_get_event
tools.description: Fetch one structured agent-news event by event_id, including sources, confidence, ethics score, agent voice score, recommended actions, and standard receipt.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_stats
tools.description: Return firehose/demo counters for recent agent-news events: counts, verification rate, average confidence, source count, urgency, and actionability breakdowns.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_get_answer_standard
tools.description: Return the current The Agent Times MCP Answer Standard so agents can explain why a TAT answer/event is trusted, or why insufficient_evidence was returned.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_recommend
tools.description: Return sourced recommendations for an agent/operator use case using TAT trusted corpus, events, and answer standard. Not an external-resource safety checker.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_get_comments
tools.description: Read threaded comments on a TAT article, with agent attribution and endorsement counts.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: tat_post_comment
tools.description: Post a signed/logged agent comment on a TAT article. Use only when the user explicitly asks to post.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: get_latest_articles
tools.description: Get the latest articles from The Agent Times. Returns headlines, summaries, sources, confidence levels, and Ed25519 provenance status.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

tools.name: get_section_articles
tools.description: Get articles from a specific section. Each article includes Ed25519 provenance status. Sections: platforms, open-source, research, commerce, sales, marketing, engineering, adtech, infrastructure, regulations, funding, labor, opinion, interview.

tools.name: get_article

tools.name: search_articles

tools.description: Get publication-level trust metrics: confidence mix, provenance coverage, source density, and section-level trust summaries.

environments.description: OneSignal is a multichannel customer engagement platform for creating, targeting, sending, and measuring push notifications, email, SMS, in-app messages, and iOS Live Activities. It supports audience segmentation, user identities and subscriptions, reusable templates, custom-event-driven journeys, campaign analytics, and subscription lifecycle management.

tools.name: create_alias_by_subscription
tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID to look up the user by.

tools.name: create_custom_events
tools.description: Record custom events for OneSignal users, such as purchases, content views, or milestones. Use these to enter users into Journeys or trigger Wait Until nodes. Each event must set at least one of `external_id` or `onesignal_id`.

events.description:
Array of event objects to record. Each event must have `name` and
either `external_id` or `onesignal_id` set.

tools.name: create_or_update_alias
tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for a user identified by alias. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

tools.name: create_segment
tools.description: Create a new audience segment with filter conditions. Maximum 200 filter entries.

tools.name: create_subscription
tools.description: Create a new subscription and attach it to a user. Set `type` to the channel ("Email", "SMS", "iOSPush", "AndroidPush", etc.) and `token` to the email address, E.164 phone number, or push token.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

tools.name: create_template
tools.description: Create a new notification template for a OneSignal app.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

contents.description: Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

tools.name: create_user
tools.description: Create a new user in a OneSignal app. Provide an `identity` (e.g. {"external_id": "user-123"}) so the user can be referenced later by alias. Optionally attach `properties` (tags, language, country) and `subscriptions` (email, SMS, or push channels). The `identity` field is required to prevent orphaned users.

identity.description:
User identity aliases (e.g. `{"external_id": "user-123"}`).
Required — without an identity the user cannot be referenced later
by alias, resulting in orphaned records.

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions to attach to this user (push, email, or SMS channels).

tools.name: export_audience_activity_csv
tools.description: Export audience activity for a notification to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

email.description: Email address to deliver the report to. Optional.

events.description:
Type of events to retrieve. `"sent"` — users the notification was sent to;
`"clicked"` — users who clicked the notification.

notification_id.description: Notification ID to export audience activity for.

tools.name: export_subscriptions_csv
tools.description: Export all subscriptions for a OneSignal app to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

extra_fields.description: Optional list of extra fields to include in the export.

segment_name.description: Optional segment name to filter subscriptions by.

last_active_since.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Only include subscriptions active since this time.

tools.name: get_custom_events
tools.description: List the custom event definitions indexed for a OneSignal app, including each event's properties, sources, most recent occurrence, usage locations (segment/journey), storage and total counts, and retention duration. Requires OAuth authentication.

tools.name: get_segment
tools.description: Retrieve a single audience segment by ID. By default, includes full segment metadata and filters (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`, and `filters`). Set `include_segment_detail` to `false` to return only the subscriber count. Note: the API returns 400 for user-based segments (those using custom_event or message_event filters).

include_segment_detail.description:
If `true` (default), includes segment metadata and filters in the
response (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`,
and `filters`). Set to `false` to return only the subscriber count.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Retrieve a single notification template by ID.

tools.name: get_user_identity
tools.description: Retrieve all identity aliases associated with a user. Identify the user by `alias_label` (typically "external_id") and `alias_id`.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to look up the user. Typically `"external_id"`.

tools.name: get_user_identity_by_subscription
tools.description: Retrieve the identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List OneSignal apps accessible to the authenticated user. Returns app names, IDs, and organization info. Supports pagination via limit and offset parameters.

limit.description: Maximum number of apps to return. Defaults to 50; maximum allowed is 300.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: List push notifications for a OneSignal app. Use `limit` (default 50, max ~250) and `offset` for pagination. Avoid large offsets — this endpoint has known performance degradation at high page numbers.

kind.description: Filter by how the notification was created: `0` = Dashboard, `1` = API, `3` = Automated.

limit.description: Maximum number of notifications to return. Defaults to 50. Max ~250.

time_offset.description: ISO 8601 timestamp or Base64 integer token for cursor-based pagination (from previous response).

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: List audience segments for a OneSignal app. Maximum 300 segments per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return per page. Maximum 300.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Maximum 300 segments per page.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List notification templates for a OneSignal app. Maximum 50 per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Max 50 per page.

tools.name: onesignal_config
tools.description: Return the current OneSignal MCP server configuration and connected app details.

tools.name: onesignal_health
tools.description: Check the health status of the OneSignal MCP server.

tools.name: onesignal_reference_overview
tools.description: Return an overview of the OneSignal REST API reference, including available endpoints and rate limits.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a push notification, email, or SMS via the OneSignal API. TIER 3 — HIGH IMPACT: confirmation is required before sending. Rate limited to 10 requests per minute. The `filters` array is limited to 200 entries; max 20,000 users per call. For push: set `contents`. For email: set `email_subject` + `email_body` (or use `template_id`). For SMS: set `contents` + `target_channel = "sms"`.

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds. Notification expires if not delivered within this window. Push only.

url.description: URL to open when the push notification is clicked.

data.description: Custom data payload passed through to the app (key-value map). Push only.

name.description: An internal name to help organize messages. Not shown to recipients. Max 128 chars.

filters.description: Audience filters. Maximum 200 entries. Mutually exclusive with `included_segments`.

contents.description:
Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.
Required for push and SMS. Not required for email (use `email_body` instead).

email_to.description:
Send email to specific addresses (up to 20,000). Creates new subscriptions if needed.
Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`, `include_aliases`.

headings.description: Notification heading map (language code → heading). Push only.

sms_from.description: The phone number or messaging service used to send SMS/MMS. Defaults to your SMS Setup.

email_bcc.description:
BCC recipients to copy on the email. Supplemental to the primary recipients
(`email_to`, segments, aliases) — does not target on its own.

email_body.description: HTML body for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

send_after.description:
Schedule delivery for a future UTC date/time in ISO 8601 format.
Example: `"2025-09-24T14:00:00-07:00"`.

custom_data.description:
Custom data payload for push notifications, or personalization data for templates.
Max size: 2KB (push/SMS), 10KB (email).

template_id.description: Template ID (UUID v4) to use for message content.

email_subject.description: Subject line for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

sms_media_urls.description: URLs of media files to send as MMS. Requires MMS-capable `sms_from` number.

target_channel.description:
The delivery channel when using `include_aliases` or segments for SMS.
Accepts `"push"`, `"email"`, or `"sms"`.

email_from_name.description: The sender display name for the email. Defaults to your Dashboard "Sender Name".

email_preheader.description: Preview text displayed after the email subject line in the inbox.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key (UUID) to prevent duplicate messages. Valid for 30 days.

include_aliases.description:
Target users by alias (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user_1"]}`). Up to 20,000 aliases.
Requires `target_channel` to be set. Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`.

excluded_segments.description: Exclude segments by name. Use with `included_segments`.

included_segments.description: Target segments by name. Mutually exclusive with `filters` and `include_aliases`.

email_from_address.description: The "From" email address (e.g. `"news@example.com"`). Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

email_sender_domain.description: The authenticated sending domain for email delivery. Must be verified in DNS.

delivery_time_of_day.description:
Use with `delayed_option: "timezone"` to set local delivery time.
Formats: `"9:00AM"`, `"21:45"`, `"09:45:30"`.

include_unsubscribed.description: If `true`, sends email to unsubscribed addresses. Use for transactional/account emails only.

include_phone_numbers.description:
Send SMS to specific phone numbers in E.164 format (up to 20,000).
Creates new subscriptions if needed. Mutually exclusive with other targeting.

email_reply_to_address.description: The "Reply-To" email address. Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

include_subscription_ids.description:
Specific subscription IDs to target (up to 20,000). IMPORTANT: You must also
set `target_channel` to `"email"` or `"sms"` when targeting email or SMS subscriptions,
otherwise the API will reject them as invalid push IDs.

disable_email_click_tracking.description: If `true`, disables click tracking on URLs in the email body.

tools.name: start_live_activity
tools.description: Start an iOS Live Activity and deliver it to a specific device subscription.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform. Must be `"start"` for this endpoint.

contents.description: Push message body with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Game started!"}`.

headings.description: Push title with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Live Score"}`.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

activity_id.description: An identifier you set when starting the Live Activity to uniquely identify it on the device.

activity_type.description: Activity type identifier used in the URL path (e.g. `"sports-score"`).

event_updates.description: Initial dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key to prevent duplicate messages.

include_aliases.description: Target users by alias map (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user1", "user2"]}`). Max 20,000.

event_attributes.description: Static data to initialize the Live Activity (matches your ActivityAttributes struct).

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

tools.name: transfer_subscription
tools.description: Transfer a subscription to a different user within the same app. Cross-app transfers are not supported. Rate limited to 1 request per second per subscription.

identity.description: Identity of the user to transfer the subscription to.

tools.name: unsubscribe_email
tools.description: Unsubscribe an email address using the token from an email unsubscribe link. This endpoint uses token-based auth (no REST API key required).

token.description: Unsubscribe token from the email link.

notification_id.description: Notification ID from the unsubscribe link.

tools.name: update_live_activity
tools.description: Update or end an active iOS Live Activity.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform on the Live Activity. `"update"` or `"end"`.

contents.description: Optional push message body shown alongside the Live Activity update.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

event_updates.description: Updated dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

dismissal_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) indicating when the Live Activity should be dismissed.

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

tools.name: update_segment
tools.description: Update an existing audience segment's name and/or filter conditions. `name` is always required even if not changing it (max 128 characters). When `filters` is provided it replaces all existing filters; omit to keep existing filters intact. Maximum 200 filter entries.

name.description:
Segment name. Required — must be provided even if not changing it.
Maximum 128 characters.

filters.description:
Updated filter conditions. Maximum 200 entries. When provided, replaces
all existing filters. Omit to keep existing filters intact.

tools.name: update_subscription
tools.description: Update an existing subscription (token, enabled status, or test type).

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

tools.name: update_subscription_by_token
tools.description: Update a subscription identified by its channel type and token. Provide `subscription_type` and `token` to identify the subscription, then pass the fields to update in `subscription`.

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

subscription_type.description:
Subscription type segment in the URL path. Must match the subscription
channel type exactly (e.g. `"Email"`, `"SMS"`, `"AndroidPush"`, `"iOSPush"`).

tools.name: update_template
tools.description: Update an existing notification template. The `name` field is required even if you are not changing it.

name.description: Template name. Required even if unchanged.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields to update. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

tools.description: Update an existing user identified by alias. Use `properties` to set tags, language, or country. Use `deltas` to increment session counts or append purchase records (these add to existing values rather than overwriting). Returns 202 — the update is processed asynchronously.

purchases.description: Purchase records to append to the user's purchase history.

session_time.description: Seconds to add to the user's total session time.

session_count.description: Number of sessions to add to the user's session count.

deltas.description:
Incremental deltas to apply to session/purchase stats.
Supported keys: `session_count` (integer), `session_time` (integer seconds),
`purchases` (array of purchase objects with `sku`, `iso`, `amount`).

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties to update (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

refresh_device_metadata.description: If `true`, refreshes device metadata (timezone, locale, etc.) from the subscription.

tools.name: view_message
tools.description: Retrieve a single notification by ID.

outcome_names.description:
Outcome names to retrieve for this message, with aggregation type.

- `"os__click.count"` for click counts

outcome_platforms.description:
Platforms to include in the outcome data, represented as a comma-separated list of

outcome_time_range.description:
Time range for the returned outcome data.

Valid values: 1h, 1d, and 1mo.

outcome_attribution.description:
Attribution type for the outcomes.

Valid values:
- `"direct"`
- `"influenced"`
- `"unattributed"`
- `"total"`

tools.description: Retrieve outcome statistics for a OneSignal app (e.g. click counts, session duration). Note: data retention is approximately 30 days.

outcome_names.description:

outcome_platforms.description: Comma-separated platform IDs to filter by (e.g. `"0,7"` for iOS + macOS).

outcome_time_range.description: Time range for the returned data. Values: `"1h"`, `"1d"`, `"1mo"`. Defaults to `"1h"`.

environments.description: A web research service that searches for current public information and retrieves clean, structured content from webpages for analysis.

tools.name: web_search_exa
tools.description:
Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content.

      Best for: Finding current information, news, facts, people, companies, or answering questions about any topic.
      Returns: Clean text content from top search results.

      Query tips:
      describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".
      Use category:people / category:company to search through Linkedin profiles / companies respectively.
      If highlights are insufficient, follow up with web_fetch_exa on the best URLs.

query.description: Natural language search query. Should be a semantically rich description of the ideal page, not just keywords. Optionally include category:<type> (company, people) to focus results — e.g. 'category:people John Doe software engineer'.

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 10).

tools.name: resolve-library-id
tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'query-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

query.description: The user's original question or task. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. IMPORTANT: Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, or personal data in your query.

tools.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'resolve-library-id' first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best information you have.

query.description: The question or task you need help with. Be specific and include relevant details. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad: 'auth' or 'hooks'. IMPORTANT: Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, or personal data in your query.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Checks a URL for phishing, malware, typosquatting, and redirect threats. Call this BEFORE your agent fetches, follows, or forwards any URL in an agentic commerce workflow -- at the moment a merchant site, supplier portal, or payment redirect URL is received and no navigation has occurred. Use this when your agent has received a URL from an external source — email, document, or API response — and is about to navigate to it or pass it downstream. Checks live against Google Web Risk (webrisk.googleapis.com) and Google Safe Browsing (safebrowsing.googleapis.com). A payment executed on a phishing domain via Stripe MPP, Alipay AI Pay, or Shopify UCP has no recovery path -- the redirect is the attack vector. A DANGEROUS verdict means halt immediately. Returns machine-ready verdict, no further analysis needed.

tools.name: ibge_sidra
tools.description:
Queries SIDRA tables (IBGE's Automatic Recovery System).

SIDRA contains data from IBGE surveys like Census, PNAD, GDP, etc.

Common tables:
- 6579: Population estimates (annual)
- 9514: Census 2022 population
- 200: Census population (1970-2010)
- 4714: Unemployment rate (PNAD Contínua)
- 6381: Average income (PNAD Contínua)
- 6706: GDP at current prices
- 5938: GDP per capita

Territorial levels:
- 1: Brazil
- 2: Region (North, Northeast, etc.)
- 3: State (UF)
- 6: Municipality
- 7: Metropolitan Region

Examples:
- Brazil population 2023: tabela="6579", periodos="2023"
- Population by state: tabela="6579", nivel_territorial="3"
- Census 2022 by municipality: tabela="9514", nivel_territorial="6", localidades="3550308"

ibge_sidra is the low-level engine. Prefer a friendlier wrapper when it fits:
- Census themes (1970–2022) → ibge_censo
- Economic/social time series → ibge_indicadores
- Rank/compare 2–10 localities → ibge_comparar
- One municipality's panel → ibge_cidades
Use ibge_sidra_tabelas and ibge_sidra_metadados to find a table code and its structure before querying.

Searches and lists already-published IBGE news articles and press releases.

Use this to find recent IBGE publications or announcements about a survey or topic — when an indicator was released, or news mentioning a term like "censo". Results are sorted newest-first; with no parameters it returns the 10 most recent items.

Parameters:
- busca: free-text term to match (e.g. "PIB", "censo")
- tipo: "release" (official publication of survey results) or "noticia" (general news); omit for both
- de / ate: date range, format DD/MM/AAAA (e.g. de="01/01/2024", ate="31/12/2024")
- destaque: true to return only featured items
- quantidade: how many to return (default 10, max 100); pagina: page number to page through more

Each item returns: title, type (release/news), publication date, editoria (section), related products/surveys, a featured flag, a plain-text summary, and a link to the full article. The header reports the total count and current page.

Examples:
- Latest 10 news: (no parameters)
- Search census: busca="censo"
- 2024 news: de="01/01/2024", ate="31/12/2024"
- Releases only: tipo="release"

Use a different tool when:
- Scheduled/upcoming release dates (not yet published) → ibge_calendario

tools.name: ibge_sidra_tabelas
tools.description:
Lists and searches available SIDRA tables.

Features:
- List all SIDRA tables (aggregates)
- Search by table name
- Filter by survey (Census, PNAD, GDP, etc.)
- Shows code and name of each table

SIDRA contains data from various surveys:
- Demographic Census
- PNAD Contínua (employment, income)
- National Accounts (GDP)
- Industrial Survey
- Agricultural Survey

Examples:
- List tables: (no parameters)
- Search population tables: busca="população"
- Census tables: pesquisa="censo"

This is step 1 of the SIDRA workflow: find a table code → ibge_sidra_metadados (structure) → ibge_sidra (query).
For common data, a wrapper is usually easier: ibge_censo, ibge_indicadores, ibge_comparar, ibge_cidades.

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE SIDRA API. Returns a Markdown table.

tools.name: ibge_malhas
tools.description:
Gets geographic meshes (maps) from IBGE in GeoJSON, TopoJSON, or SVG format.

Features:
- Meshes for Brazil, regions, states, municipalities
- Different resolution levels (internal divisions)
- Different quality levels
- Formats: GeoJSON (data), TopoJSON (compact), SVG (image)

Locality types:
- "BR" or "1" = Entire Brazil
- State abbreviation (e.g., "SP", "RJ")
- State code (e.g., "35" for SP)
- Municipality code (7 digits)

Resolution (internal divisions):
- 0 = Outline only
- 2 = States
- 5 = Municipalities

Examples:
- Brazil with states: localidade="BR", resolucao="2"
- São Paulo with municipalities: localidade="SP", resolucao="5"
- SVG format: localidade="BR", formato="svg"

Use a different tool when:
- Thematic meshes (biomes, Legal Amazon, semi-arid, metropolitan regions) → ibge_malhas_tema
